subtitle: What the ligeng0197/graphmemix release pipeline actually executes. Lane = canonical stage (METHODOLOGY-SKELETON §2.2); empty lanes mean the stage does not exist here.

footer: memory-bench · methodology flow · code view · every citation re-opened and confirmed during verification
legend_notes: A3 ADMIT stays empty in code too — the only fact-storage-time dedup is a memory_id idempotency guard (_ingest:339), not a similarity-based P-DEDUP; no P-CONFLICT, no P-EVICT, no training anywhere.

The node-utility fusion the paper writes as one formula next to the verifier call is a separate script in a later pipeline stage here, with logistic-regression coefficients fit on gold labels via a 5-fold SHA256 dev split — a calibration protocol the paper never describes, and the numbers do not equal the paper's stated (0.8, 5.2, 0.7) even 'up to displayed rounding'.

The paper's unconditional 'execute in parallel' claim for the two verifiers does not hold: the ecv stage requires node stage's persisted candidate_ids + query_captions cache before it can run at all, and the conditional query-image-caption LLM call only ever fires inside the node stage.

Constructing ConcreteMemixMethod (checkpoint / priors / reader stages) unconditionally requires an external private repo, vendor/memix-core, that ships nowhere in this repository, its README, or its docs — three of the nine pipeline stages cannot run without it (task-specific confirmation, §5-A of verification.md).
